paper.title_en: Separation of gravitational perturbations of Myers--Perry black holes
paper.abstract_en: Gravitational perturbations of higher-dimensional rotating black holes generally obey coupled partial differential equations, making their separation a longstanding challenge. We separate linearized gravitational perturbations of nonextremal, asymptotically flat five-dimensional Myers--Perry black holes with two nonzero spins of unequal magnitude and arbitrary azimuthal numbers. The Killing--Yano symmetry induces a first-order angular operator that, together with a commuting second-order operator, determines the angular profiles of all five gauge-invariant curvature components. The joint angular harmonics form a complete basis at real frequencies, and all five components of each separated mode share a single radial amplitude satisfying a second-order scalar equation obtained through the Carter interchange. The corresponding metric perturbations can be reconstructed locally. We further extend this angular structure to Myers--Perry black holes in arbitrary dimensions with nonzero spins of pairwise distinct magnitudes. Second-order symmetry operators associated with the Killing tensors induce mutually commuting angular operators on all curvature polarizations, with coefficients independent of radius. In odd dimensions, a Killing--Yano three-form generates an additional first-order angular operator commuting with this family. This common angular structure provides a route toward complete separation of gravitational perturbations in higher-dimensional rotating black holes.
